title: DNS propagation window surge mitigation cheatsheet
summary: Quick reference for operators to reduce user impact during DNS-driven regional shifts and short TTL propagation windows. Focuses on pragmatic mitigation tactics when DNS records are slow to converge or when client-side caching causes microbursts after a failover.
incident_context_and_problem_statement: Observed multiple incidents where regional evacuation + low TTL changes resulted in a 3-8 minute window of elevated 5xxs and client retry amplification. Root cause pattern: a subset of clients (mobile SDKs, some CDNs) ignored updated short TTLs or re-resolved only on connection teardown, causing uneven load on target regions and hot spots in warm standby capacity.
key_hypotheses:
1) Client DNS resolvers that follow OS caching semantics hold records for longer than configured TTLs, especially on Android.
2) Edge/CDN attachments with long connection reuse re-resolve less frequently; long-lived connections concentrate traffic.
3) In-flight KV cache and session affinity cause amplification when a fraction of clients switch, creating microbursts.
4) Route propagation (cloud provider BGP) can lag, so even after DNS change some egress paths still land on old region for minutes.
operational_goals_for_mitigation:
- Keep user 99th p90 latency within SLO during shifts.
- Avoid token-costly fallbacks and repeated retries.
- Smooth per-region QPS ramp during DNS convergence.
- Keep tail error increase <2x baseline for any 5-minute window.
playbook_quick_steps:
1) Confirm scope: run 'incident-scope' query (team-runbooks) to identify affected zones and client types.
2) If failover in progress, hold any further DNS edits.
3) Temporarily increase warm-standby capacity by +25-50% in target region (autoscale override).
4) Enable connection-draining helpers: apply TCP connection-timeout policy on edge (30s) to encourage re-resolve on client reconnect where safe.
5) Incrementally shift weighted route: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100% with 2 minute observation windows.
6) If 5xx spike persists at first step, abort further weight increases and roll back to last stable weight.
7) Notify SDK/product to push a lightweight config that forces re-resolve for problematic clients (where supported).
8) If DNS still not converging after 10 minutes, enable fallback regional proxy layer (egress rewrite) for sensitive routes.
detailed_checks_and_commands:
- Verify DNS record change: dig +trace @8.8.8.8 example-api.redwood.ai A.
- Check TTL observed by public resolvers: dig +short @1.1.1.1 example-api.redwood.ai soa && dig +nocmd +nostats +nocomments +nocmd example-api.redwood.ai TTL.
- Inspect edge connection reuse: kubectl exec -it edge-proxy-xx -- netstat -anp | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l.
- Warm standby scaling: airflow trigger_dag scale_warm_standby --region us-west-2 --delta 50
- Weight shift API: curl -X POST $ROUTER_API/weights -d '{"target":"us-west-2","weight":10}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'
- Connection-drain: patch-ingress --set connectionTimeout=30s --target edge-pool
metrics_and_alerts_to_watch:
- regional_error_rate_5m (alert at >3% over baseline)
- regional_p95_latency (alert at >2x baseline)
- edge_connection_reuse_ratio (watch for >80%)
- kvcache_miss_rate_after_shift (expect spike; if >30% sustained then investigate cache warmup)
- route_weight_spread (verify weights applied match controller state)
- DNS_ttl_observed (compare observed TTL across probes: >configured TTL indicates caching)
decision_points_and_rollbacks:
- If error rate spikes >5% during any weight step: rollback to previous stable weight and pause 10 minutes.
- If client re-resolve rate <20% after connection-timeout change: push SDK config or consider long-term client mitigation.
- If BGP path convergence issues suspected (traceroute shows old region for >5 minutes): engage cloud provider support and consider adding temporary edge-reroute via dedicated proxies.
comms_and_notifications_template:
Short channel message for #oncall: 
Title: Region shift in flight (us-west-2) — monitoring
Body: We applied DNS failover at 14:07 UTC. Shifting weights to us-west-2 incrementally (10% -> 25%). Observed p95 +35% and error rate +1.8% (within tolerance). Autoscaling warm-standby +30% requested. Watching 2-minute windows; next update at 14:11 UTC. Contact Asha for ops.
Include: link to runbook, JIRA-8891, metrics dashboard URL.
post_incident_followups:
- Add client SDK telemetry: track time of last DNS re-resolve and connection reuse.
- Run a controlled chaos test that simulates TTL-ignored clients to validate weighted ramp plan.
- Evaluate edge config change to prefer shorter connection reuse for API endpoints during planned failovers.
- Update runbooks to include explicit CDN vendor docs (Akamai/CloudFront behaviors) and example TTL observations.
- Create an experimental lightweight push for mobile SDKs that triggers a DNS refresh on next cold start.
open_questions_and_unknowns:
- Exact percentage of clients that ignore short TTLs across major app versions. Need sampling.
- Impact of regional DNS over HTTPS (DoH) providers on re-resolve frequency.
- If we implement forced re-resolve SDK setting, what's the rollout risk for users on flaky connections?
notes_for_postmortem_section: Collect timeline of: DNS edit time, router controller apply time, observed weight distribution, first error spike timestamp, kvcache miss amplification period. Correlate with CDN and ASN-level traces. Include sample client logs showing stale DNS IP usage where possible.
